detail.problem: Parts judged: (a) presenting complaint 'breast symptoms' -> task due_to (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Breast finding" "finding")): correct. (b) 'temperature >= 38C' -> (>= (measurement (snomed_concept "Body temperature" "observable entity") °C) 38): correct. (c) 'or body pain' -> (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Generalized aches and pains" "finding")): acceptable concept, but note the recorded common symptom is 'Muscle pain', which is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of 'Generalized aches and pains' (checked), so body pain recorded as Muscle pain will not satisfy this rule. (d) 'painful lump in breast/s' -> (and Breast lump, Pain of breast): reasonable approximation. (e) 'may be fluctuant': missing (see parts_missing). (f) 'breast abscess likely' -> probable (snomed_concept "Abscess of breast" "disorder"): correct. (g) logic (fever OR body pain) AND painful lump: correct. (h) 'Give urgent attention' -> Urgent priority via (active_condition Abscess of breast): correct and matches the house pattern for a red box that names a likely diagnosis.
Minor: 'may be fluctuant' not encoded (optional wording). 'Breast symptoms' and 'painful lump' captured as Breast lump + Pain of breast; temp >=38 or body pain captured as OR.

ref: Diagnose probable breast engorgement / Diagnose probable blocked milk duct / Diagnose probable mastitis associated with lactation / Diagnose probable mastalgia
text: All four use (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Pain of breast" "finding")) as the 'painful breast/s' evidence. In SNOMED, 'Sore nipple' and 'Painful lactation' are direct children of 'Pain of breast', and descendants match in due_to. The page's left branch ('Breastfeeding and painful/cracked nipples') is deliberately separate from 'painful breast/s with or without lump/s', yet a breastfeeding patient recorded with sore nipples alone would receive probable engorgement and probable blocked duct (afebrile) or probable mastitis (febrile). Nothing in the file checks for or excludes nipple pain.

Most of it is expressible (Dimpling of surface of breast, Peau d'orange surface of breast, Breast symptom of change in skin, Family history of malignant neoplasm of breast, Nipple discharge symptom, Bloody nipple discharge, Axillary lymphadenopathy, Retraction of bilateral nipples all exist); age and sex are not. The page names no diagnosis and 'refer same week' matches no priority level, so omitting a rule is defensible, but the check_for prompts for none of these findings, and nipple discharge and axillary lump (two of the page's five presenting complaints) occur nowhere in the file.

text: 'Body pain' is encoded as (snomed_concept "Generalized aches and pains" "finding"). The system's recorded common symptom for body/muscle pain is 'Muscle pain', which is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of 'Generalized aches and pains' (checked). A patient whose body pain is recorded as Muscle pain will fail the fever-or-body-pain test in both rules and, if breastfeeding and afebrile, fall through to probable engorgement/blocked duct instead of mastitis. Either add Muscle pain as an alternative or use the common-symptom concept.

The diagnosis concept (snomed_concept "Pain of breast" "finding") is identical to one of its own evidence findings, so the rule records as a probable diagnosis the very finding the nurse entered. ref: Diagnose probable mastitis associated with lactation
text: Overlaps with the abscess rule: a breastfeeding patient with a painful lump and fever/body pain satisfies both, so the system will output probable mastitis (clinic flucloxacillin) and probable breast abscess (urgent surgical referral) at once. The page's lower algorithm is headed 'Approach to the patient with breast symptoms not needing urgent attention', so mastitis is meant only for patients who do not meet the red box; the page's own discriminator is weak ('which may be fluctuant'). The grammar does not allow (no (active_condition ...)), so this cannot be excluded cleanly. This reproduces an ambiguity on the page rather than inventing one; it should go to a clinician. The concept is right: plain 'Mastitis' does not exist in SNOMED and the rule already requires breastfeeding.

The diagnosis concept 'Pain of breast' is the same concept as one of its own evidence findings, so the rule restates a recorded finding as a probable diagnosis. SNOMED has no better general concept (mastalgia is a synonym of 'Pain of breast'; 'Cyclical mastalgia' and 'Non-cyclical mastalgia' are narrower than the page). The not-breastfeeding, breast pain, exam-normal conditions are faithful to the page. Worth confirming that VHA wants a probable diagnosis that equals its evidence.
